name: Filipino Ginisang Monggo with Spinach and Rice

components.name: Ginisang Monggo

ingredients.name: DRY whole green mung beans rinsed and sorted
Water for cooking dry mung beans

steps: Rinse and sort dry whole mung beans; simmer in measured water until tender, 35-55 minutes depending on batch and age.
Meanwhile saute onion, tomato and garlic in oil until fragrant and tomatoes soften.
Add the diced squash and a ladle of bean cooking liquid; simmer until the squash is almost tender.
Mix the cooked mung beans and remaining liquid into the vegetables; season with salt and soy sauce instead of fish sauce.
Stir spinach through for the final 2-3 minutes; avoid overcooking it.

components.name: Jasmine Rice
steps: Cook rice separately and divide monggo and rice into five portions. This is a meatless version: the original includes pork/shrimp/fish sauce.

Source Panlasang Pinoy recipe includes pork, shrimp, fish sauce and stock cube; ALL replaced/omitted to meet veggie category. Source handling: Source technique/reference; measured UNHANGRY complete-meal adaptation.
Planning: Soak mung overnight to shorten cook if desired.
Freezer: mung bean stew and rice freeze well
Dietary: Soy; no fish, pork, shrimp or meat stock in THIS adaptation.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (≤4°C); refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers, freeze portions for later in the week, and reheat to at least 74°C.
